recipes.name: Lemon Cooler Cream Cake
ingredients_raw: 2 (3 ounce) packages lemon flavored Jell-O® mix
1 (3.4 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix
1 (8 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Combine cake mix, 1 cup water, eggs, and oil in a large bowl; beat with an electric mixer on low speed until moistened. Increase speed to medium and beat for 2 minutes. Pour batter into the prepared baking dish. Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, 21 to 26 minutes.

Poke holes all over top of cake with a fork. Combine 1 cup hot water and remaining 1 cup cold water with 1 package gelatin powder; stir until gelatin is dissolved. Pour mixture over cake. Chill in refrigerator until cool.
Stir milk, pudding mix, and remaining 1 package gelatin powder together in a large bowl until powders dissolved. Fold in whipped topping; spread over cake. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Lemon Cooler Cream Cake
raw_recipe.description: This lemon cooler cream cake combines boxed cake mix, lemon gelatin, vanilla pudding, and milk, then topped with whipped topping and served cold.

video.description: Tart and sweet lemon cake! Add a creamy pudding topping for true decadence!

review.reviewBody: This has been a hit everytime I make it. My family loves it. One mistake I made ended up being a great change to the recipe. I accidentally bought lemon pudding mix instead of vanilla and it added that extra tartness that everyone said was missing. I also made the icing while the cake was baking and put it in the fridge to firm up until the cake was cool enough to be iced. I find it is not as unstable. I also cut the water to the gelatin to 1 cup which also made a difference. This has been a big winner at summer family cookouts. I am from Houston TX and I don't think you could experience a hotter more humid summer. That being said, I make sure that I take extra care when I plan on taking it to any function in the summer months. This cake is better if made the night before and refrigerated until the next day, as it gives it time to set and firm up. If I am transporting it I use an insulated carrier (fits a 9x13 pan) I also understand they make one for layer cakes or I make sure it stays in the ice chest until ready to serve. I also improvised before by putting it in a box and wrapping it in two huge bath towels with zip lock bags of ice packed around it. This cake is definitely meant to be set out when you are ready to serve it. Some might find this as being too much effort, but I love the recipe and I don't mind taking the time.

This was my second time making this cake. I reduced the amount of water to one cup (1/2 boiling & 1/2 cold), to mix with first jello box. Much better amount this time-no soggy cake. Took about two hours to fully set up & be ready for the topping. As for the topping; I only had lime jello left and vanilla pudding—WOW!!! That was an AMAZING change! Thanks to everyone sharing their tips!!

Baked cake according to instructions and added 1 extra egg, replaced water with milk and added 1 tsp of vanilla. When adding the lemon jello mixture, 1 only added 1 cup of water as instructed by other reviews. The recipe did not state when to add the jello/water mixture to the cake.
I let sit 15 to 20 mins after taking out of oven and poked holes and spooned over the jello mix. Let cake cool and put in frig. For the frosting recipe,
mixed milk, lemon pudding mix, and lemon jello- mixed well, then added 1 -8 oz pkg of sofeten cream cheese, mixed with mixer then added juice of one whole lemon, mix well, then folded in the whipped topping - let set overnight in frig - yum

Before making I read several reviews both pro and con. I bought all the ingredients but did not use them all. Recipe calls for two packages of lemon jello but I only used the one to poor over the cake and I only used about 34 of it. I was worried all of it would make the cake too soggy. When I made the frosting with the CoolWhip combined with vanilla pudding I omitted the second package of lemon jello. I did refrigerate for two hours before serving. It came out wonderful. Not too sweet not too lemony and perfectly moist. It was served after a heavy brunch meal of quiche, crab cakes, fried chicken, shrimp salad, etc. Everyone remarked how refreshing it tasted after a heavy meal. Glad I made the few small changes.

I added fresh squeezed lemon juice for half of all the water. Next time, even though more involved, I'd like to make the pudding from scratch. Also, in the future, I will be sure to pour the (instant) pudding on more quickly, before it starts setting up. 
This dessert was a hit with everyone, including my husband and my family that came for Easter dinner. I made two 8x8 pans instead of one 13x9 and took the 2nd pan to a sew day with friends. Luscious lemony flavor without being overly tart. It was extra delicious chilled from the refrigerator. Will make it again!

This one is another keeper! Moist and very flavourful. Delicious!
I used the suggestion of someone that used the lemon-flavoured pudding rather than the vanilla pudding. GREAT suggestion!

Also, I added two egg yolks for extra "like homemade than a box cake mix" texture. 

Instead of Cool Whip, I used whipped cream to make the icing/topping. It may be a few more calories, but we don't have dessert often.
 The family enjoyed this ending to a fine dinner.

We loved it! 
Instead of Cool Whip (or the like) I used real whipping cream, and omitted the milk. I whipped the cream first, then added the pudding and jello. 
For esthetics, I grated lemon rind on top. 
Yum!

My favorite easy cake.
I have made about 10 times. I keep adding lemon. 
Is awesome as is but I reduced water to one cup also with jello. Was afraid after reading reviews to add 2 cups on the cake.
I add more sugar free lemon jello, lemon zest and lemon extract to the cake and the topping. 
Thanks for this. Recipe.
Just tried everything in orange. Is great too. The lemon is lighter and the orange taste a bit like an orange creamsicle. 

Excellent recipe!

Overall the cake and topping were delicious! The cake did seem a little bit too moist, so when I make it again I will use only 1 cup total instead of 2 cups with the gelatin on the cake. I didn’t have instant vanilla pudding on hand for the topping, so I used instant lemon instead and it was VERY good! My family loved this cake!
This was delicious, my daughter loves lemon cake and this was easy and awesome! I also used lemon pudding in place of the vanilla pudding, it turned out perfect!!!
Absolutely yummy. Used lemon pudding. Cut down water a bit adding in the juice from 1 lemon with it. I served it at Easter the day after it was made. Ate every bit and still tasty day 3.

This is a nice variation on the classic poke cake. As several reviewers suggested, I reduced the water in the gelatin to 1/2 cup boiling and 1/2 cup cold. I also subbed lemon pudding for the vanilla. Very refreshing!
Super easy to make and very delicious. The cake is so airy and delicate. Lovely lemon flavour, not tó strong. Big winner in our house.
So Good! So lite! NEW FAMILY FAVORITE

My granddaughter loves this cake, but she likes it in an orange flavor. I use the same recipe, with orange jello. I add 1 tin mandarin oranges to the topping. You can also put a cup of miniature marshmallows in the fluff topping. Very versatile and delicious recipe.
If you like lemon, then this is a recipe for you. Very easy to make and the topping makes it a winner. I will repeat this one often.
The cake and frosting were good. Way too much frosting for the 9X13. Still searching for an amazing lemon desert.

Easy and very delicious! Everyone i served absolutely raved about it and were begging for leftovers. I also used only 1 cup of water with the jello and only used lemon pudding and whipped topping for my icing. This one is a crowd pleaser and def a keeper!

I loved the fresh tartness of this cake recipe. It was easy to make, and I think I'll be adding this to my family's rotation. However, the kids' only complaint was that it was TOO moist. I may ease up on the jello-water liquid next time. But the flavor is perfect! NOTE: I added lime zest to give it a lemon-lime aroma, but it turned out looking like sour cream and onion dip, so I'll switch to lemon zest next time.
I gave this four stars only because I like my lemon desserts more tart. If you love lemons and sweet, you will love this
